The true positive rate is 32%, indicating that around 3 out of 10 samples belong in this category.In this zone, the main feature is the EGR1 gene. However, there are two other genes involved: the DUSP family (dual specificity phosphatases) and the GRB2 protein. We can say that EGR1 is differentially expressed in this group. The literature confirms that EGR family members have been shown to play key roles in mediating stress responses through regulation of both transcriptional and posttranscriptional processes . In addition, they have also been implicated in tumorigenesis, angiogenesis, metastasis, and drug resistance . Therefore, EGR1 could be playing a role in mediating the stress response, but further research needs to be done to determine whether it is associated with the outcome of interest.The literature supports the association of Fos with EGR1 . Fos protooncogene encodes a member of the AP-1 transcription factor complex. Studies have found that the overexpression of Fos leads to increased proliferation of breast cancer cells , and its expression correlates with the expression of another gene, JUN, in the human breast cancer cell lines MCF-7 and SKBR3 . It has also been reported that overexpressing Fos in normal mammary epithelial cells leads to increased cell proliferation . This suggests that Fos plays a significant role in breast cancer progression.Another interesting observation is the inverse correlation between Fos and Dusp6. As stated earlier, DUSPs are dual-specificity phosphotyrosine phosphatase enzymes. There is evidence that DUSP4 can dephosphorylate ERK, thereby inactivating the MAP kinase pathway and inhibiting cell growth . Another study showed that DUSPs regulate the activity of several phosphokinases involved in cell growth control, such as CDKs, MAP kinases, and RTKs . These findings suggest that DUSPS may be important regulators of cell growth and proliferation.Grb2 is part of the SH2 domain family, which binds to phosphotyped residues and plays a critical role in cellular signal transduction. Grb2 has been found to mediate mitogen-stimulated tyrosine phosporylation of c-fos and c-jun . The activation of c-jnk is necessary for the induction of apoptosis, and therefore it seems likely that grb2 may play a similar role.The literature does not support the link between Fos, DSPU6, and GRB2. However, studies have shown that Fos and Jun are activated in response to epidermal growth factor (EGF) stimulation . Furthermore, studies have identified Fos and Egr1 as downstream targets of the Janus kinase (JNK) signaling pathways . Together, these findings suggest that Fos, Jun, and Egr-1 may all be involved in the same pathway in response to growth factors.

In response to extracellular stimuli, Fos forms heterodimers with Jun proteins, such as c-Jun, to regulate the transcription of downstream genes involved in cell proliferation, differentiation, apoptosis, inflammation, stress responses, and immune regulation. Dusp1 is a dual-specificity MAP kinase phosphatase that specifically dephosphorylates p-ERK1/2 and p-JNK, thereby regulating the MAPK/ERK and MAPK JNK pathways, respectively. These pathways play important roles in controlling cell growth, survival, migration, differentiation and apoptosis. Grb2 is a multidomain adaptor protein that binds to activated receptor tyrosine kinases and regulates several signal transduction pathways, including the RAS/MAPK and phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/AKT pathways. Rps6kb1 is a ribosomal protein S6 kinase beta-1 that belongs to a family of serine/threonine kinases. It plays a key role in the control of translation initiation through its ability to phosphorylate ribosommal protein S6.LITERATURE CONFIRMED MECHANISM: c-FOS , DUSP , Ribosome Protein S6 Kinase beta-family members have been reported to be involved in breast cancer progression. [25–27]. For example, c-fos promotes tumourigenicity and metastasis of basal-like breast carcinoma . In addition, inhibition of Ribosomal Protein S4 kinase beta1 suppresses the invasion and migration of breast cancer cells .New Testable Mechanisms: c-JUN, a member protein of the activator protein-1 (AP-1) complex, which can induce various types of human cancers, has been identified as a potential therapeutic target for breast cancer treatment .
